problem: VLN training data from simulators lacks scene diversity and real-world complexity. Web room-tour videos are a rich source, but explicit COLMAP reconstruction fails on most of them (about 17K of ~200K candidate trajectories succeed, >90% lost), which limits usable geometry-aware data.
motivation: Agents need diverse, realistic, spatially aware supervision to generalize, and web videos offer continuous human walking trajectories in thousands of real homes. Since SfM is fragile on blurry, dynamic, low-overlap footage, spatial cues should be obtained directly from RGB with a learned geometry model, so that discarded videos can be reused.
key_idea: Build RoomTour3D from web room-tour videos (description-enriched and COLMAP action-enriched trajectories, with GPT-4 instructions), then add a frozen VGGT-based spatial encoder that supplies implicit geometry features to NaviLLM for videos where explicit reconstruction is unavailable.
insight: Implicit and explicit geometry are complementary: implicit-only beats explicit-only on CVDN and R2R (7.07 vs 6.33 GP; 64 vs 62 SPL), is slightly worse on SOON and REVERIE, and combining both gives the best results on all four benchmarks (Table ab_igr). Because implicit geometry removes the reconstruction filter, all trajectories can be used for geometry training, which gives a further gain (R2R 64→66, REVERIE 38.0→39.2). The information ablation shows that object tags, depth/box and room type each add value to the summarization data.
method: Video collection and filtering: 1,847 YouTube room-tour videos (243 h), filtered with GPT-4 on titles and descriptions, a minimum length of 3 min, and a transition detector; downscaled to 360 px and sampled at 3 fps.

Description-enriched trajectories: frames are sampled every 2 s; BLIP-2 gives room type (16 classes, smoothed), RAM gives object tags, Grounding-DINO gives boxes, Depth-Anything gives depth; the outputs are textualized as left/center/right and near/medium/far, and GPT-4-Turbo writes open-vocabulary trajectory descriptions (~100K trajectories, 200K captions).

Action-enriched trajectories: COLMAP reconstruction on 100 s overlapping clips, merged by DFS over the overlap graph; view-change points (>45° angle change) are selected with NMS and DBSCAN, giving a positive (most recent) frame and a negative (largest angular deviation) frame per cluster (17K trajectories).

NaviLLM training tasks: a summarization pretraining task (frames as cand tokens, generate the trajectory description) and an action-selection finetuning task (frames as candidates, history tokens, STOP token), on top of the NaviLLM multitask mixture.

Spatial encoder (IGR): the transformer blocks of a pretrained VGGT without heads produce frame-wise implicit geometry embeddings; a spatial projector maps them into LLM space and replaces the explicit pose/distance encoder for web video, while simulator data keeps explicit distance/heading.

IGR training: initialized from RoomTour3D weights, the projector is randomly initialized, the spatial encoder is frozen, projector and LLM are trained (lr 5e-6, 5000 steps) on simulator plus all web-video data.

setting.backbone: NaviLLM (Vicuna-7B-v1.1 with EVA-CLIP-02-L scene encoder, fine-tuned) + frozen VGGT spatial encoder
setting.training_data: RoomTour3D (~100K description trajectories, 200K captions, 17K action trajectories from 1,847 videos) plus CVDN, SOON, R2R, REVERIE, ScanQA, LLaVA-23k and augmented R2R/REVERIE data
setting.observation: panoramic RGB from the simulator; monocular video frames for web data
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph candidate view selection (plus STOP)
setting.privileged: none at test time (REVERIE uses the benchmark-provided object boxes)

results: RoomTour3D-IGR improves over the reproduced NaviLLM baseline on all four benchmarks, e.g. R2R val-unseen SPL 57→66, REVERIE 31.4→39.2, SOON 28.0→32.7, CVDN GP 6.09→7.38. It also sets new zero-shot R2R results for open-source 7B models (SR 19.21 / SPL 14.60, versus 0 for NaviLLM without action data), and it is more robust to visual degradations.
limitations: The pipeline builds on NaviLLM and relies on GPT-4-generated descriptions of moderate quality (average relevance 3.08/4) and on noisy tagging and depth models.
Zero-shot performance is still far below GPT-4-based agents (DiscussNav SR 43, MapGPT SR 43.7).
Evaluation is limited to discrete-graph simulator benchmarks with no real-robot or continuous-control tests, and some comparisons use reproduced baselines and integer-rounded R2R numbers.
